title: A new murmur after mechanical valve replacement / Do not miss haemolysis or endocarditis

blocks.text: A new murmur after mechanical valve replacement / Do not miss haemolysis or endocarditis

AMaC MRCP PACES · R5-110 · Physical examination · PACES Station 3, cardiovascular · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 examination, at least 4 questions) · Guideline dates and links in section 15 · Related AMaC: condition may appear elsewhere in a different context.
A patient with a mechanical mitral valve has become breathless and tired. Examine the cardiovascular system to establish the likely cause.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
HOOK — A new regurgitant murmur beside a prosthetic valve with anaemia makes paravalvular leak plausible, not proven.
EXAMINER TRAP — Do not label every new mechanical-valve murmur as expected flow; urgently consider endocarditis and prosthetic dysfunction.

RELEASED FINDINGS — on inspection, pulse, precordial palpation and auscultation as appropriate: Mechanical mitral valve, new apical pansystolic murmur radiating to axilla, pallor, no fever, no peripheral endocarditis signs; mild ankle oedema.
Question 1 [R4] — Why does she have anaemia? | Mechanical shear haemolysis: check LDH, haptoglobin, bilirubin, film.
Question 2 [R5] — How confirm leak? | TTE first; TOE often essential to characterise paravalvular location.
Question 3 [R6] — What must be excluded? | Prosthetic valve endocarditis and valve obstruction.
Question 4 [R7] — When intervene? | Symptomatic/significant regurgitation or haemolysis requiring transfusion; Heart Team.
Curveball — If a candidate asks for definitive proof from examination alone: “Explain what examination suggests and which confirmatory tests you need.”

A new regurgitant murmur beside a prosthetic valve with anaemia makes paravalvular leak plausible, not proven. Do not label every new mechanical-valve murmur as expected flow; urgently consider endocarditis and prosthetic dysfunction. Mechanical shear haemolysis: check LDH, haptoglobin, bilirubin, film. TTE first; TOE often essential to characterise paravalvular location. Prosthetic valve endocarditis and valve obstruction.

THINK: Paravalvular leak with haemolysis.
SAY: A new regurgitant murmur beside a prosthetic valve with anaemia makes paravalvular leak plausible, not proven.
DO: Consent, focused cardiovascular examination, present findings and next tests.
NUMBERS: 10-minute examination encounter (PACES23).
TRAP: Do not label every new mechanical-valve murmur as expected flow; urgently consider endocarditis and prosthetic dysfunction.
FINISH: Explain definitive investigations and appropriate specialist follow-up.
